questions.q: Who was the founder of the Maratha Kingdom?
questions.a: Shivaji was the founder of the Maratha Kingdom. A wrong answer here suggests the student has not yet associated the name "Shivaji" with the origin of this specific regional power.

questions.q: How did Shivaji’s relationship with the Bijapur Sultanate and the Mughal Empire change over his lifetime?
questions.a: He moved from serving these powers as a local chieftain to actively taking their forts and territories to build his own kingdom. If a student says he always served them, they misunderstand his role as a founder who fought for independence.

questions.q: If you were a local leader in the 17th century, what steps would you take to establish your own kingdom like Shivaji did?
questions.a: Steps: (1) Identify a region to control, (2) secure defensive locations like forts, (3) gain the support of local people, and (4) declare independence from existing rulers. A wrong answer focuses only on fighting, ignoring the importance of local support and defensive planning.

questions.q: Compare a local chieftain serving an empire to a Chhatrapati. What is the fundamental difference in their power?
questions.a: A chieftain follows the orders of an emperor, while a Chhatrapati is an independent king who makes his own laws and governs his own land. Students failing this comparison do not grasp the transition from vassal to sovereign ruler.

questions.q: Is it accurate to say the Maratha kingdom was always an independent power from its very beginning? Why?
questions.a: No, it is not accurate because Shivaji started his career serving the Deccan Sultanates before he built his own independent kingdom. A student who says "yes" misses the historical context of his rise from a local position.

questions.q: Create a title for a story about how a local leader becomes a king. What one event would be the climax?
questions.a: The title should reflect growth or independence, such as "The Rise of the Mountain King." The climax should be his coronation in 1674, as that is when he officially became Chhatrapati. A weak answer lacks a clear connection to his transition from local leader to king.
